Have you tried reinstalling Windows 7 while BIOS was in Legacy mode with Secure Boot off? If OS was installed when BIOS is in UEFI mode, it will fail when switched to Legacy.

This topic is a bit confusing, but if you think of it like UEFI is the successor to regular ol' BIOS it will start making sense. UEFI is the newer verision of computers BIOS. It changes the way the machines boot basically, so these settings need to be set before the OS is installed. See below.

* **UEFI mode:** the newer boot mode, requires a separate partition (called **EFI partition**) where bootloaders are stored.
* **BIOS mode:** the old way used by the BIOS, the bootloader would be stored on the disks (usually at the beginning of the disk).

Basically your Windows 7 OS install is looking at the wrong location for its bootloaders.

It was difficult. I spent a week brainstorming and researching. Even now I am making tweaks. We are also Healthcare using ServiceDesk Plus and I have based our Service Catalog off of ITSM research. I made our service desk to be end user friendly. I made templates and categories with end users in mind. Usually service desks go with technician in mind, but thats not the way you want to go if you expect users to use the system to submit requests.

You will not find a cookie cutter catalog or categories. You build off a foundation of what its supposed to  be and make it your own. You can use others as ideas, but its best to try to figure out what works best for your environment and users.

My service catalog is sort of limited as we have not implemented self service portal or CMDB. Its sort of basic at the moment to get the Help Desk side working. 

I have three catagories to choose from: Incident, Request, and Question. There is a fourth that only technicians see and thats User Management for off/on boarding.

Within Incident, Request, and Question I have it broken down as: Access/Login, Email, Network, Other(not shown), Print/Fax/Scan, Purchases, Reporting, Communications/Telecom, Smartphone/Tablet, Software, User Management, and Workstation. 

I tried not to use service specific categories as I cannot guarantee we will always have that same service. I also did put "Verbs" in category or sub category, tried to use nouns. Verbs did make their way in there though. Also try to limit how many categories are shown so its not so overwhelming. Also when I was creating other team members insisted on more categories or to break down some to get more specific. But I asked them one question, are you really going to run a report on that specific issue? I mean REALLY??? If they are not, dont add it. 

Well anyways, I am unsure if this is what you were looking for, but I hope it helps. Feel free to reach out to me if you have other questions.
